text:
The biggest story in Tampa isn't on the scoresheet. Nikita Kucherov told the Lightning on Oct. 30 that he won't re-sign and asked for a trade, according to an AP source, and he has since said the request comes from disrespect and a lack of communication. General manager Julien BriseBois has said he has no intention of trading him. Kucherov keeps playing and scoring all the same, with nine goals so far.

The team around him is very good. Tampa Bay is 15-6-2 with 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against) and a 56% share at 5v5, and its 32 points are only 3.1 above what its play has earned. Our race model gives the Lightning a 95% playoff chance and a 44% shot at the Atlantic. The Kucherov, Jake Guentzel and Brayden Point line has outscored teams 11-4, and John Carlson's pairing with Charle-Edouard D'Astous has 63% of the expected goals and a 17-6 goal edge. Erik Cernak has 8 points in 10 games against 3.2 expected.

The concerns are fresh. Brandon Hagel went on injured reserve last week with an upper-body injury, and Sunday's 6-2 home loss to Buffalo was a rough end to a 7-3-0 stretch.

What to watch: how long Hagel is out, and whether the Kucherov standoff stays quiet while the wins keep coming.
headline: The Lightning keep winning while Kucherov wants out
